subject: physics_2
question_text: Define modulation. Why is it necessary?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Whether Communication Systems is still on the current Telangana second-year syllabus is UNCONFIRMED — NCERT removed this chapter in the 2023 rationalisation, but this book prints it. A lecturer's pen tick marks this question as expected. Physics hand-checked: modulation combines a low-frequency message signal with a high-frequency carrier by varying the carrier's amplitude, frequency or phase; it is needed because an antenna must be of the order of λ/4 (kilometres long at audio frequency), a low-frequency antenna radiates very little power, and modulation lets signals travel far and keeps different transmitters from mixing — the book's four reasons, all correct.

recall_prompt: Define modulation in one sentence, then give the reasons it is necessary — the antenna size argument is the one to include.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
steps.mark_note: Message signal combined with a carrier
lines: Modulation is the process of combining a
high-frequency carrier wave, so that the
amplitude, frequency or phase of the
carrier changes according to the signal.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Low-frequency message, high-frequency carrier, and what changes.
steps.why: The definition must name both signals and their roles: the message is low frequency and cannot travel well on its own, the carrier is high frequency and can — modulation puts the message onto the carrier by changing one of the carrier's properties.
common_mistakes: Saying two signals are added. The carrier is not added to the message; one of its properties is VARIED according to the message.
Swapping the roles. The message signal is the low-frequency one; the carrier is the high-frequency one.

recall.must_convey: That modulation combines a low-frequency message signal with a high-frequency carrier by varying the carrier's amplitude, frequency or phase according to the signal.
accept: the message signal is put onto a high-frequency carrier
a property of the carrier is varied according to the signal
combining the audio signal with a high-frequency wave

steps.memory_tip: Low onto high: the low-frequency message is carried by the high-frequency wave.

steps.label: Why it is necessary
steps.mark_note: Antenna size is the key reason
lines: 1. To send signals over long distances.
2. To keep the antenna size practical — an

lines.text: antenna needs a length of about λ/4, and
an audio frequency would need one many

lines: 3. Because an antenna radiates very little

lines.text: Modulation: message signal onto a carrier

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two clear reasons are enough; the λ/4 antenna argument is the strongest.
steps.why: All four reasons trace back to frequency: an antenna works well only when its length is about a quarter of the wavelength, and at audio frequency λ is hundreds of kilometres — so the signal must be moved to a high frequency, where the antenna is short, the radiated power is useful, and each transmitter can be given its own band.
common_mistakes: Writing λ/4 as λ/2 or 4λ. The working antenna length is about a quarter of the wavelength, λ/4.
Giving only 'to travel far' with no reason. The antenna-size argument is what earns the mark.
Saying modulation removes noise. It does not; noise still enters in the channel.

recall.must_convey: That modulation is needed because an antenna must be about λ/4 long — impossibly long at audio frequency — and low frequencies radiate little power and would mix between transmitters.
accept: the antenna must be about a quarter wavelength
an audio-frequency antenna would be kilometres long
low frequency radiates very little power
it stops different transmitters from mixing
reject: a property of the carrier is varied

steps.memory_tip: Four reasons, one root: distance, antenna size, radiated power, no mixing — all fixed by raising the frequency.

insider_note: One mark for the definition — both signals named with their roles — and one for the necessity, where the λ/4 antenna argument is the reason examiners look for.
